newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen awaiting jobless data.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen awaiting jobless data.

text.p: The direction of Wall Street stocks at the market open Friday will depend on the U.S. jobs report, but yesterday's gains could provide a boost, analysts said.

The unemployment data, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, will provide initial direction to bonds and stocks. But a strong rebound by technology issues on Thursday could help lift stocks at the open, analysts said.
Jobs data are expected to show nonfarm payrolls increased by 219,000 jobs in May, compared to gain of 142,000 in April.
The unemployment rate is expected to rise to five percent from April's 4.9 percent. Average hourly earnings are seen up 0.4 percent after dropping 0.1 percent in April.

"The numbers due at 0830 (EDT/1230 GMT) are the key," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal. "The speculation is for a little pickup in the unemployment rate and the addition of over 200,000 new jobs."
This would be favorably received by both bonds and stocks, he said.
A decline in the unemployment rate would trigger inflation and interest rate fears, he said.

"There is apprehension now about the July FOMC meeting," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood. "The unemployment data will bear on that apprehension one way or another."
He said markets would react astrongly only if the data showed a surprising gain or fall in U.S. unemployment.
The market is still more concerned with negative earnings preannouncments, Brown said.

"I don't think these (jobs) numbers are that important," said James Cramer, president of Cramer Berkowitz & Co. "If they are strong, this will be the last strong number." He believes the economy is starting to slow.
Battipaglia said, "Based on yesterday's valiant rally by technology stocks...I'd predict a higher open."
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 0.80 point at 846.85, while the long bond was up 1/32 at a 6.88 percent yield.

On Thursday, stocks took an optimistic view of the U.S. unemployment and interest rate outlook, with the Dow industrials finishing up 35.63 points at 7305.29. Technology stocks clawed back from recent weakness, and Nasdaq closed up 10.38 points at 1390.05.
Japan's Nikkei-225 index finished off 2.40 points at 20485.75. In London, the FTSE 100 was up 30.4 points at 4606.6. U.S. stocks were steady there as European investors awaited the U.S. jobs data.
The dollar retraced lows against the yen in Tokyo, trading at 115.70/80 yen. In Europe it was at 1.7380/90 marks.
The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that individual investors would be interested in buying derivatives based on the 30-stock Dow industrials.

The New York Times said in its Market Place column that the New York Stock Exchange plan to start trading stocks in dollars and cents could mean savings for investors, but some savings could be offset by higher commissions.
